{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Screening visit overloaded with many procedures",
      "quote": "Pulmonary function test",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The screening visit includes a large number of assessments, including pulmonary function test, which may be time-consuming and burdensome for patients. This could impact recruitment and retention.",
      "fix": "Consider moving pulmonary function test to a separate baseline visit or reducing other screening procedures to alleviate patient burden."
    },
    {
      "title": "Tumor tissue sample at progression may be difficult to collect",
      "quote": "Tumor tissue sample taken at pre- treatment, on-treatment,and at disease progression (optional, only if part of the SoC)",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Collecting tumor tissue at disease progression is often challenging in practice, as patients may not undergo biopsy as part of standard of care. This could lead to missing data for exploratory endpoints.",
      "fix": "Clarify that this is optional and consider alternative collection methods (e.g., liquid biopsy) to ensure feasibility."
    },
    {
      "title": "Multiple blood samples on C1 Day 1 may be excessive",
      "quote": "Blood sample for plasma biomarker assessment and diagnostic development(eg, ctDNA and blood- based biomarkers) (mandatory)",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "On Cycle 1 Day 1, there are multiple mandatory blood samples (plasma biomarkers, gene expression, exploratory clinical benefit/safety, PK pre- and post-dose, ADA). This is a high burden for patients and may be logistically challenging for sites.",
      "fix": "Consolidate blood draws where possible or reduce the number of mandatory samples on the first treatment day."
    },
    {
      "title": "Troponin only at screening and EOT may miss on-treatment cardiotoxicity",
      "quote": "Troponin",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Troponin is only assessed at screening and end of treatment, but T-DXd is known to have cardiac toxicity. More frequent monitoring may be needed to detect early cardiac injury.",
      "fix": "Add troponin assessments at multiple on-treatment timepoints (e.g., each cycle) to align with cardiac safety monitoring."
    },
    {
      "title": "Ophthalmologic assessment only at screening and EOT may miss ocular toxicity",
      "quote": "Ophthalmologic Assessment",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Ophthalmologic assessment is only at screening and end of treatment, but T-DXd has been associated with ocular adverse events. More frequent monitoring may be needed.",
      "fix": "Consider adding ophthalmologic assessments at regular intervals during treatment to monitor for ocular toxicity."
    },
    {
      "title": "Eligibility criteria checked at C1 Day 1 but not at later cycles",
      "quote": "Eligibility criteria",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Eligibility criteria are only checked at screening and C1 Day 1, but patients may develop conditions that affect continued participation. However, this is standard practice.",
      "fix": "No change needed, but ensure that any changes in eligibility status are captured through adverse event monitoring."
    },
    {
      "title": "High Resolution Chest CT at screening only may miss early progression",
      "quote": "High Resolution Chest CT",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "High Resolution Chest CT is only at screening, but tumor assessments are not scheduled until later (not shown in SoA). This may delay detection of progression in the chest.",
      "fix": "Ensure that tumor assessments include chest CT at regular intervals as per RECIST 1.1, and clarify in the SoA."
    },
    {
      "title": "ePRO and pulse oximetry device allocation only on C1 Day 1 may cause delays",
      "quote": "ePRO and pulse oximetry device allocation (ePRO device allocated only if patient does not have own compatible device) and training",
      "page": 18,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Device allocation and training on Cycle 1 Day 1 may be time-consuming and could delay treatment initiation. Also, if the patient does not have a compatible device, additional logistics are needed.",
      "fix": "Consider providing device and training during screening or a separate baseline visit to streamline Day 1 procedures."
    }
  ]
}
